excerpt_original: The filmmaker was chosen by the jury for the Film London-sponsored £10,000 prize from an all-female shortlist.

blocks.alt: Black and white film still showing two men, one older, in traditional Indian attire, turning to look at the younger, wearing a western-style suit
blocks.caption: Alia Syed, Fatima’s Letter , 1992, film still. Courtesy the artist

blocks.text: Alia Syed, described as a ‘master of analogue filmmaking’, has won the the Jarman Award. The London and Glasgow-based artist started her career working with the London Film-Makers Co-operative in the 1980s; and recent projects mine her family history and themes of migration and memory. Oral histories and the stories Syed has heard from her parents and grandparents are central to her practice: Snow (2019), for example, uses Hi8 footage shot by her father; while The Dhaba ( 2025) is a portrait of two men who migrated to Glasgow from the Indian subcontinent in different periods.

Syed was chosen by the jury for the Film London-sponsored £10,000 prize from an all-female shortlist that included Sadia Pineda Hameed, and her investigation of radical soundscapes; Ilona Sagar and her film Other Actors (2025), a portrait of Paimio tuberculosis sanatorium in Finland; and Rhea Storr’s filmic portrait of Black community spaces in the UK.

The jury, which featured Woodrow Kernohan of the John Hansard Gallery; the BFI’s Luke Moody; artist Hope Pearl Strickland; Whitechapel Gallery director Gilane Tawadros and Eve Gabereau, Director of Distribution at Vue International, who described Syed as ‘A pioneer of experimental film and artists’ moving image, the beauty and compelling nature of her work which touches on questions of memory and migration among others, is combined with a deep understanding of and inventiveness with the craft of filmmaking. A master of analogue filmmaking, she continues to show a restless will to play, experiment and change, wholly befitting of a Jarman Awardee.’
Films by the four shortlisted artists are on show at the Whitechapel Gallery through 13 December .
